author: TEDx Talks
description:
We’re living longer than ever before, but are we living well? Dr Meghan Dares explores the growing gap between lifespan and healthspan, revealing how small losses in movement can quietly reshape our future. Through the story of one patient who just wanted to dance again, she challenges us to rethink pain, ageing and what it really means to stay alive. 

Dr Meghan Dares is an orthopaedic surgeon and co-founder of Joint Vision Orthopaedic Group in Wollongong. She specialises in joint preservation and lower-limb reconstruction, combining advanced surgical techniques with research into movement longevity. Her work centres on a simple belief: protecting mobility is essential to protecting independence, identity and quality of life. Through her clinical practice and research, she advocates for a shift in how we think about ageing - not just extending lifespan, but strengthening healthspan. Her mission is to help Australians age well by protecting the strength and mobility that underpin inde
title: Why preserving your mobility is key to healthy aging | Meghan Dares | TEDxWollongong

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Life’s biggest questions present themselves to us whether we want them to or not. When we try to answer them, we tend to go wrong in three familiar ways: dogmatism, where certainty shuts inquiry down; moral relativism, where we seek our culture or religion’s answer and avoid the harder question of whether that answer is right; and nihilism, where the search for answers is abandoned altogether.  Drawing on years of facilitating dialogue, Dr. Yarmel shows how a collaborative and rigorous search for truth through inquiry dialogue can help us make genuine progress on the questions that shape our lives.
 Dr. Aaron Yarmel is the Associate Director of the Center for Ethics and Human Values and an award-winning lecturer in the Department of Philosophy, and the Director of the Philosophy for Children Academy at Ohio State. His research focuses on philosophy for children, AI ethics, social change, and two-level utilitarianism. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format
title: How (not) to answer the questions that keep you up at night | Aaron Yarmel | TEDxOhioStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What remains after unimaginable loss? Photographer Lou Bopp reflects on documenting the bedrooms of children lost to school shootings and explores how photographs can preserve memory, create empathy, and help us confront absence in profoundly human ways. Through images that reveal what words cannot, he invites us to consider how we remember - and why it matters.

The Oscar®-winning All the Empty Rooms is a seven-year project with Steve Hartman, CBS News, and Joshua Seftel, Director.

TEDxStLouis is dedicated to discovering, developing, and sharing ideas that positively impact St. Louis and beyond. Since 2013, TEDxStLouis has produced more than 200 talks reaching millions of viewers worldwide. Learn more at TEDxSaintLouis.org  Lou Bopp is an on-location commercial photographer specializing in lifestyle photography of people and pets, with an aesthetic approach that blends honesty, texture, and connection to create compelling moments for some of the world’s biggest brands.

He has multi
title: A Photographer of Absence  | Lou Bopp | TEDxStLouis

author: TEDx Talks
description: After a childhood and early adolescence of feeling like there was no space for her to belong, coming out and moving to Columbus, Ohio, offered Julia solace for the lifelong yearning for community. It was here that she found a bar that would save her life… twice. For marginalized communities, the magic of the space where people come together over a shared identity has been lost, and with it, a sense of belonging.  Dr. Julia M. Applegate is a Senior Lecturer in the WGSS Department, as well as the Director and Producer of the upcoming documentary Free Beer Tomorrow, telling the story of Ohio’s oldest lesbian bar. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: This bar saved my life… twice | Julia Applegate | TEDxOhioStateUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Caught in the crossfire of a shooting near campus after a record-breaking season, Nathan shares not only the path back to health, but also the shortfalls and setbacks. He posits that recovery is a marathon, not a sprint, and while the journey may not be perfect, it’s important to take time to discover the treasures in the dark.  
 Nathan Demian is a student-athlete and captain of Ohio State Men’s Soccer. Shortly after winning the 2024 Big Ten championship, he was caught in a shooting. Demian was able to overcome what could have been a fatal injury and return to the field this past season. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The shot that ended my season – and started my life | Nathan Demian | TEDxOhioStateUniversity

Their energizing songs bring together faith, understanding, and acceptance for audience members to listen to.  The African American Voices Gospel Choir's purpose is to foster an on-campus environment where students can come together to celebrate through music and the arts, contributing to a diverse, urban community while striving for academic excellence and sharing the African American tradition with others. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: In her speech, "Before the Dream Begins," Ruchika Chaubal shares her grandfather's story and the legacy he left for her family. She explores the ideas of mindset, determination, and consistency. Chaubal describes her family's journey and its impact on her life. She highlights the growth mindset and consistent hard work that inspire her to pursue her dreams. Ruchika Chaubal is a junior at Olentangy Liberty High School. She is the assistant field commander of Liberty’s marching band, a member in mock trial, and co-president of Asian Student Association. She competes in all types of dance at Powell Dance Academy where she is a senior premier dancer. Through volunteering at a local senior home for 3 summers and registering people to vote through voter service events, Ruchika strives to serve her community in all ways possible. title: Before the Dream Begins | Ruchika Chaubal | TEDxOlentangy Liberty Youth

description:
Diagnosed with cancer at 15, Amelia Howe dismantles the "battle" and "fight" language wrapped around the illness and shows how it quietly strips young patients of control and dignity. 

A clear-eyed, deeply personal call to change how we talk about cancer and let people navigate it on their own terms.

TEDxBristol 2025 was held at We The Curious, Bristol's much-loved science centre on the city's historic harbourside, and beautifully filmed and edited by the team at Watch & Learn Productions (watchandlearnproductions.com).

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx Amelia Howe was diagnosed with cancer at 15 and has since become a powerful advocate for changing how we talk about the illness.

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker explores the transformative power of reimagining familiar places—from abandoned factories and forgotten recreational spaces to historic communities like Haghpat. Just as a fresh interpretation of a beloved song can make us appreciate the original all over again, breathing new life into existing spaces can reconnect us with our roots, our communities, and the land we call home. The buildings are still there. The memories remain. Perhaps the future begins not by erasing the past, but by learning to see it differently. Karine Bagdasaryan is an architect and educator based between Barcelona and Yerevan, currently teaching in the Master of Architecture program at La Salle University and collaborating with an architecture office in Barcelona. She holds a Master’s degree in Architecture with distinction from ETSALS (2023) and has studied and worked internationally in Armenia, Russia, Latvia, and Spain. Her work includes the Contemporary Cavern Pavilion in Riga and h

She highlights the importance of embracing questions over certainty, showing how a curious mindset opens doors to new perspectives and deeper understanding. Through engaging insights, this talk encourages audiences to challenge assumptions, stay open to discovery, and recognize that meaningful progress often begins with a single question. description: In "From Ideas to Impact: Turning Imagination into Real-World Solutions," Shaurya Singh explores how bold ideas can become meaningful solutions when paired with curiosity, creativity, and action. Drawing on innovative thinking and practical problem-solving, he encourages audiences to move beyond imagination and take the first steps toward creating positive change. This talk inspires viewers to see challenges as opportunities and demonstrates that every impactful innovation begins with a single idea. Shaurya Singh is the founder of NewYuv Technologies, an AI-Powered Solutions and Digital Marketing Service provider for businesses. Driven by a passion for technology and entrepreneurship, he established the company to build customised software that is easy to use and enhances efficiency, and to also provide marketing solutions for businesses to generate leads for selling their products. description: In "The Courage to Be Different: The Day I Stopped Waiting for Permission," Saurya Tiwari shares a powerful perspective on embracing individuality and breaking free from the fear of judgment. Through personal experiences and thoughtful insights, he encourages audiences to stop seeking external validation and start making choices that align with their values and aspirations. This inspiring talk reminds us that true growth begins when we have the courage to be ourselves and take the first step without waiting for permission. Saurya T. is a Grade 11 student whose curiosity lies at the intersection of endurance, mindset, and personal growth. At just 16 years old, he became the youngest person in Bangalore to complete a 54-kilometre marathon, but he believes the most meaningful part of that journey had little to do with running. His experiences taught him how easily we wait for permission from society, from expectations, and even from ourselves before pursuing what truly matters. In his TE

Through thought-provoking insights and practical perspectives, she encourages audiences to shift their focus from acquiring more to creating with intention. This talk inspires viewers to redefine success, embrace innovation, and choose purpose over possessions, demonstrating that lasting impact comes from what we create, not what we own. Anvita Srivastava is an avid reader and a passionate writer. Her love for writing began when she was about one third of her current age- and soon evolved into a form of expression for her. From occasional journal entries to winning multiple writing competitions, she now has two novels to her name - an anthology “Pills of Chills”, and her first solo debut novel - “A Leafy Affair”.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Many of us spend our lives answering the question, "What do you want to be?" But what if we've been asking the wrong question all along? In this thought-provoking talk, Pino Di Ioia challenges our focus on titles, achievements, and career paths, encouraging us instead to ask, "Who will you become?" Drawing on research, personal insights, and powerful real-world examples, he explores why character, resilience, empathy, and purpose are the true foundations of a meaningful life. By shifting the conversation from what we do to who we are, Pino invites us to rethink how we define success—for ourselves and for future generations.
 What began as a summer job during his MBA turned into a decades-long journey of building joy, one pastry at a time. Pino was the brand’s first franchisee, first area developer, and now serves as CEO and co-owner of BeaverTails — one of Canada’s most iconic indulgent brands. Alongside his twin brother and wife, he’s grown the company from a beloved treat to a coast
title: Who will you become? | Pino Di Ioia | TEDxSt Laurent Blvd

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often believe that if we explain the facts clearly enough, people will change. But what if information alone isn't enough? In this thought-provoking talk, Laura François explores why today's interconnected crises are also crises of broken relationships. Drawing on systems thinking, neuroscience, philosophy, and the concept of awe, she invites us to rethink how meaningful change happens—not only through understanding, but through connection. Rather than asking how we solve complex problems, Laura asks a deeper question: how do we restore our relationship with each other, ourselves, and the living world? Laura François is an impact strategist, writer and the Director of Awe Exchange, a nonprofit laboratory based in Montreal and Ho Chi Minh City. Her work focuses on how awe and relational intelligence can reshape approaches to complex systems, particularly in climate adaptation and emerging technologies. 

For nearly a decade, Laura has worked across Southeast Asia and Canada with org
title: Why we need systems feeling | Laura François | TEDxSt Laurent Blvd

description:
“Life is beautiful. Dream big, take action, and surround yourself with the right people.” 

Inspired by the story of Yasuke, the first African samurai who earned the trust of Oda Nobunaga, David shares his own journey of arriving in Japan with a bold vision but no clear roadmap. Through moments of doubt, small steps forward, and meaningful encounters, he discovered that dreams are not built on status or background, but through the relationships we cultivate. His talk explores how shared vision and human connection turn ambition into reality.  David Christian Kpondehou, known as the “African Samurai,” is a Beninese entrepreneur and founder of Africa Diaspora Network Japan (ADNJ). Living in Japan for nine years, he works to strengthen connections between Africa and Japan through business, cultural exchange, and youth empowerment. Alongside training with the Centre for Investigative Journalism, Sonya has built experience across television, radio, and digital media, working with broadcasters including ITV and Channel 4, while also hosting her own Doncaster-based radio show. Her talk encourages individuals to overcome setbacks, remain authentic, and continue moving forward despite uncertainty, reminding audiences that success is built through consistency and courage. description: Music is often seen as a source of entertainment, but its influence reaches far beyond playlists and performances. In this talk, Ishan Raj Onta, lead of Elements Band explores how music shapes emotions, preserves culture, strengthens communities, and serves as a powerful medium for storytelling and social change. Through personal experiences and real-world examples, he invites the audience to rediscover music not just as something we hear, but as something that influences how we think, connect, and grow. Ishan Raj Onta, the frontman of the Nepalese indie-rock band The Elements, is celebrated for his emotive vocals on hit tracks like Birsiney Hau Ki, Putli, and Tesailey Hide Ma. Before dedicating himself to music, he was a practicing lawyer and successful moot court competitor. This unique legal background gives him a sharp, captivating storytelling edge that shines through in his songwriting. description: What if the most important thing a college education gives you has nothing to do with what's taught in class? Lou Hirsch argues that higher education has spent decades optimizing away the one thing it can't afford to lose: the human moments that actually shape who we become. This talk is a case for paying attention — and a reminder that being seen by another person might be the most powerful thing education can offer. Lou Hirsch, Ph.D., is an Assistant Professor of Plant Pathology at the University of Kentucky’s Martin-Gatton College of Agriculture, Food and Environment and the inaugural Director of FIELD, a collegewide program advancing pedagogical innovation, student success, and the scholarship of teaching and learning. His career follows a nontraditional path that began in the outdoors of Arizona and a maritime career as a boat captain and scuba instructor, a vocation he has continued for 24 years. description: Most of us worry about saying the wrong thing when someone we care about is suffering. In this talk, Dr. Abigail Latimer reflects on a patient who taught her that meaningful connection is not about finding the right words, but about being willing to show up for difficult emotions. Blending personal experience with research from palliative care, psychology, and social science, she offers practical guidance for supporting others through illness, grief, and hardship. Abigail Latimer, Ph.D., MSW, LCSW, APHSW-C is an Assistant Professor in the University of Kentucky College of Social Work and College of Medicine. She is a UK College of Social Work graduate and has post-doctoral training with the University of Kentucky College of Nursing, Research Interventions for Cardiovascular Health. Dr. Latimer specializes in adapting and implementing serious illness communication interventions, with a focus on older adults with heart failure and those who are unhoused or housing vulnerable. Dr. Tagbo Niepa is the Arthur Hamerschlag Associate Professor of Chemical Engineering and Biomedical Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, where he leads an interdisciplinary research program at the intersection of biology, materials science, and engineering. After earning his bachelor’s and Ph.D. degrees in Chemical Engineering from Syracuse University, he completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Pennsylvania and previously served on the faculty at the University of Pittsburgh. Dr. Niepa’s research focuses on combating drug-resistant pathogens, advancing antimicrobial technologies, and engineering innovative platforms to study the human microbiome.
